lessons.title: The feed quality system in practice
lessons.html:
The feed quality system in practice

Quality in a feed mill means two things: the feed meets its nutritional specification, and it is safe for animals and, through them, for people who eat meat, milk and eggs. Monitoring and maintaining standards is a daily, practical task, not just paperwork.

Elements of the system

  • Specifications for every raw material and finished product: nutrient ranges, physical properties, contaminant limits.
  • HACCP plan: hazards (biological such as Salmonella, chemical such as mycotoxins and medicament carry-over, physical such as metal and glass) and the critical control points that control them.
  • Prerequisite programmes: cleaning, pest control, maintenance, personal hygiene, glass and hard plastic control, supplier approval, training.
  • SOPs and records that prove the system works.
  • Legal requirements: feed registration and labelling under Act 36 of 1947.

Sampling and testing plan

PointTypical checks
Raw material intakeMoisture, protein, mycotoxins, foreign matter, insects
GrindingParticle size
MixingMixer uniformity (CV) at set intervals
PelletingConditioning temperature, PDI, fines, moisture
Finished feedProximate analysis, key minerals, medicament level where applicable
DispatchCorrect product, label, clean vehicle

Samples must be representative, labelled and stored correctly. Retention samples of finished feed are kept for the period the procedure sets so that complaints can be investigated.

Monitoring critical control points

For each CCP there is a critical limit, a monitoring method and frequency, a responsible person, a corrective action and a verification step. Make sure monitoring is done and recorded on time, and that people know what to do when a limit is breached.

lessons.title: Acting on results and improving
lessons.html:
Acting on results and improving

Interpreting results

  • Compare each result with the specification and its tolerance.
  • Look at trends, not only single results. A protein value drifting down over several batches can indicate raw material change, scale drift or formulation error.
  • Use simple control charts where possible to see when a process is going out of control before it breaches the limit.

When results are out of specification

  1. Place affected product on hold and identify all affected batches.
  2. Check the result: was the sample representative, was the test done correctly? Retest if justified.
  3. Investigate the cause: raw material, weighing, mixing, process conditions, equipment.
  4. Decide the disposition with management: release with concession, rework, downgrade or destroy.
  5. Record corrective and preventive actions and check they work.

Verifying the system

  • Calibration: scales, thermometers, moisture meters and lab instruments on schedule.
  • Internal audits: check that SOPs are followed and records complete; raise findings.
  • Mock recalls: trace a finished product back to raw materials and forward to customers within the target time.
  • Supplier evaluation: review suppliers on quality, delivery and certificates of analysis.
  • Hygiene inspections: cleaning standards, pest activity, glass and hard plastic register.

Complaints

Treat every customer complaint seriously: record it, collect samples and information from the farm, check retention samples and batch records, find the root cause and respond. Feed complaints are often about animal performance, which can have many causes, so investigate carefully and objectively.

Building a quality culture

Train operators on why quality checks matter, involve them in investigations, recognise good practice and make it easy to report problems without fear. Quality is everyone's job.

Key points

  • Quality means meeting specification and being safe.
  • HACCP identifies hazards and controls them at critical control points.
  • Sample representatively, keep retention samples and watch trends.
  • Hold, investigate, decide and correct when results are out of spec.
  • Verify with calibration, audits, mock recalls and complaint investigation.
